findings.where: Hero, the action row: the filled blue 'Write to me' button and the underlined address 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com' beside it (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The page's one action does nothing. 'Write to me' looks like a filled primary button, and a hover rule picks it out, but it is not a link or a button. The underlined address next to it is not a link either. The only working mailto is the small address in the footer, at the very bottom of the page. A visitor who clicks either hero element gets no response, and nothing on the first screen tells them where else to go.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided to contact Mark. They click the obvious button, or the address that looks like a link, and nothing happens. Some will copy the address by hand; many will conclude the site is broken and leave. Mark loses the one thing the homepage exists for (brand sheet §1).

findings.where: Hero, the action row: 'Book a consultation' beside 'Write to me' (desktop; on phone it is stacked under the address)
findings.fault: The first screen has two primary actions with equal weight: two identical filled blue buttons. The brief asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark. 'Book a consultation' is a link to #consult, and no consultation or booking section appears anywhere on the page. It promises a booking flow that a brochure site with no bespoke software does not have.
findings.who_objects: A visitor ready to make contact has to choose between two buttons that look the same. Those who pick 'Book a consultation', expecting a calendar or form, land nowhere or on nothing like what was promised. The founder would also object: the personal-advisor test asks for one direct way to reach him, and a booking button reads as a firm's sales funnel.

findings.where: Hero left margin: the three margin notes ('Istanbul, 2025 / Best Practices in PPP Legislation for Emerging Economies', 'Melbourne, 2026 / LLM Course…', 'São Paulo, 2024 / New Approaches to Risk Allocation…'). The same look recurs in every specimen label below ('Palette', 'Type', 'Texture', 'Article page', 'Motion', 'Tile notes')
findings.fault: The notes are set in the house blue, which the palette names as the link colour. They are also titles of real talks, the kind of text a visitor expects to open. None of them links anywhere. On this page the same blue means 'link' in the footer address and 'static label' in the margin. The brief asks for blue margin notes, so this is a clash between the brief and the link colour's reserved meaning, and the founder should rule on it.
findings.who_objects: A visitor curious about Mark's Istanbul or São Paulo talk clicks the blue title and gets nothing. They learn that blue cannot be trusted to mean 'link', and may then doubt the real links too. A visitor using colour alone to find links is misled at every note.

findings.where: Motion sketch: 'Replay the entrance', compared with the footer email link
findings.fault: A button that replays the animation looks exactly like the footer mailto: blue underlined text. The same look carries two functions, one that acts on the page and one that leaves it.
findings.who_objects: Few visitors would notice. Someone reading the specimen might expect 'Replay the entrance' to take them somewhere, not to rerun the motion in place.
